subject: python
title: Loops
description: for and while, range(), enumerate(), and how break, continue and else behave.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A for loop walks over an iterable — a list, a string, a range, a file. A while loop repeats as long as a condition holds. In Python you almost always want for: it cannot run past the end of the data.

content.title: Index and value together
content.body: Reach for enumerate() instead of building an index by hand; it keeps the loop readable and off-by-one errors out.
content.code:
for i, name in enumerate(["a", "b", "c"], start=1):
    print(i, name)

# 1 a
# 2 b
# 3 c

content.title: Watch out
content.body: range(1, 5) yields 1, 2, 3, 4 — the stop value is excluded. And mutating a list while iterating over it silently skips elements; iterate over a copy instead.

exercises.question: What does this print?
exercises.code:
for i in range(1, 4):
    print(i, end=" ")
exercises.explanation: range(start, stop) includes start and excludes stop, so range(1, 4) gives 1, 2, 3.

exercises.question: What does continue do inside a loop?

answers.text: Skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one
Restarts the loop from the first item

exercises.explanation: continue jumps to the next iteration; break leaves the loop. Neither one restarts it.

exercises.question: Which line makes this loop run forever?
exercises.code:
1  n = 5
2  while n > 0:
3      print(n)
4      n = n
5  print("done")

answers.text: Line 4 — n is never decreased, so the condition stays true
Line 3 — print inside a while is not allowed

exercises.explanation: A while loop needs its condition to change. n = n - 1 (or n -= 1) is what the body is missing.

exercises.question: Complete the loop so it prints both the position and the value.
exercises.code:
for i, item in ___(items):
    print(i, item)
exercises.explanation: enumerate() yields (index, value) pairs. zip() would pair two separate iterables instead.

exercises.question: What does this print?
exercises.explanation: A loop's else block runs when the loop finished without hitting break — which is exactly a "nothing matched" search result.

exercises.question: Iterating over a string yields its characters one at a time.
exercises.explanation: A str is an iterable of one-character strings, so for ch in "abc" gives "a", "b", "c".

exercises.question: Complete the comprehension that squares every number.
exercises.explanation: A list comprehension reads expression + for + target + in + iterable, with an optional if at the end.

exercises.question: Built-in
exercises.back: Pairs two iterables item by item and stops at the shorter one
exercises.explanation: for name, score in zip(names, scores) walks both lists in step. Anything past the shorter list is dropped silently.

exercises.question: What is the final value of total?
exercises.code:
total = 0
for n in range(4):
    total += n
print(total)
exercises.explanation: range(4) is 0, 1, 2, 3 and those sum to 6. range(5) would have given 10.
